{"status":"ready","summary":"The issue's hypothesis was wrong. The lineitem OR-of-ranges filter is not a ConjunctionOrFilter. FilterCombiner::TryPushdownOrClause only builds ConjunctionOrFilter for an OR of plain comparisons, so an OR of BETWEEN/AND ranges is pushed as an EXPRESSION_FILTER and runs through ExpressionExecutor::SelectExpression. Replacing the quadratic union in CONJUNCTION_OR alone (the plan as written) moved the isolated scan only 2.62s→2.39s cumulative.

All changes are in src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp:
1. New dense-mask path (TryDenseFilterSelection), used by both EXPRESSION_FILTER and CONJUNCTION_OR. It applies when the column is numeric (int8..int128, uint8..uint128, float, double), the vector is flat (vdata.sel unset), and the filter is a tree of AND/OR over comparisons (=, <>, <, >, <=, >=) and BETWEEN between the column itself (BOUND_REF index 0, same type) and non-NULL constants of exactly the column type. Each comparison becomes one branchless loop writing a 0/1 mask, AND/OR combine the masks, and the selection is emitted in input order. If the incoming sel is non-identity, the selected values are gathered into a compact buffer first. NULL rows are dropped at the end via validity, which is correct because the tree has no NOT. Anything else falls through to the existing code.
2. CONJUNCTION_OR fallback: the O(n²) duplicate-check union is replaced by a per-row bool bitmap. Later children only see rows not yet matched, and the output keeps input order. This only applies when all sel indices are < STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE; otherwise the old loop runs (scan_count can exceed the vector size).

Measured with dbe-tool on my build:
- Isolated `count(*) WHERE OR of 3 ranges`: scan 2.32s→0.97s cumulative, 0.305s→0.134s wall. That is now the same cost as a single BETWEEN (0.97s).
- bench q19: −7.3% and −11.3% on two runs (155→144ms, 163→145ms).
- An intermediate version without the gather (masking all 2048 rows even with a sparse incoming sel) was +5.2% slower on q19 on two runs. The gather fixed that.
- bench result checks passed on every run.","generality":"This helps any table scan with a pushed-down filter on one numeric/decimal column that is an AND/OR tree of comparisons with constants, especially OR-of-ranges / OR-of-BETWEEN (ExpressionFilter), and OR of equalities or comparisons (ConjunctionOrFilter). Examples are disjunctive range predicates and the per-table OR filters derived by JoinDependentFilterRule. It does not apply to:
- VARCHAR/bool/interval columns
- non-flat (dictionary/constant) vectors
- expressions with casts, functions, IN, IS NULL, or NOT
- constants whose type differs from the column type
- vectors with more than STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE selected rows
All of these use the existing paths unchanged. Semantics match the executor: it uses the same Equals/LessThan/etc. operator templates (including NaN handling for floats), and a NULL row fails a NOT-free AND/OR tree.","notes":"- Profile ToString looks the same for ConjunctionOrFilter and ExpressionFilter. Check which TableFilterType actually reaches FilterSelection before optimizing it.
- In the scan, the OR filter often runs after more selective filters (shipinstruct eq, the bloom-filter dynamic filter), so work must stay proportional to the incoming sel. Dense evaluation of the full vector cost +5%; gathering first fixed it.
- Possible follow-up: make TryPushdownOrClause build ConjunctionOr-of-ConjunctionAnd TableFilters for OR-of-ranges. That would also enable zonemap pruning through ConjunctionOrFilter::CheckStatistics, but it is a riskier plan-level change.
- The remaining lineitem scan cost in q19 is the other filters: the string-equality filter, the optional IN filter on another string column, and the bloom-filter dynamic filter."}

structured_output.summary:
The issue's hypothesis was wrong. The lineitem OR-of-ranges filter is not a ConjunctionOrFilter. FilterCombiner::TryPushdownOrClause only builds ConjunctionOrFilter for an OR of plain comparisons, so an OR of BETWEEN/AND ranges is pushed as an EXPRESSION_FILTER and runs through ExpressionExecutor::SelectExpression. Replacing the quadratic union in CONJUNCTION_OR alone (the plan as written) moved the isolated scan only 2.62s→2.39s cumulative.

All changes are in src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp:
1. New dense-mask path (TryDenseFilterSelection), used by both EXPRESSION_FILTER and CONJUNCTION_OR. It applies when the column is numeric (int8..int128, uint8..uint128, float, double), the vector is flat (vdata.sel unset), and the filter is a tree of AND/OR over comparisons (=, <>, <, >, <=, >=) and BETWEEN between the column itself (BOUND_REF index 0, same type) and non-NULL constants of exactly the column type. Each comparison becomes one branchless loop writing a 0/1 mask, AND/OR combine the masks, and the selection is emitted in input order. If the incoming sel is non-identity, the selected values are gathered into a compact buffer first. NULL rows are dropped at the end via validity, which is correct because the tree has no NOT. Anything else falls through to the existing code.
2. CONJUNCTION_OR fallback: the O(n²) duplicate-check union is replaced by a per-row bool bitmap. Later children only see rows not yet matched, and the output keeps input order. This only applies when all sel indices are < STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE; otherwise the old loop runs (scan_count can exceed the vector size).

Measured with dbe-tool on my build:
- Isolated `count(*) WHERE OR of 3 ranges`: scan 2.32s→0.97s cumulative, 0.305s→0.134s wall. That is now the same cost as a single BETWEEN (0.97s).
- bench q19: −7.3% and −11.3% on two runs (155→144ms, 163→145ms).
- An intermediate version without the gather (masking all 2048 rows even with a sparse incoming sel) was +5.2% slower on q19 on two runs. The gather fixed that.
- bench result checks passed on every run.
structured_output.generality:
This helps any table scan with a pushed-down filter on one numeric/decimal column that is an AND/OR tree of comparisons with constants, especially OR-of-ranges / OR-of-BETWEEN (ExpressionFilter), and OR of equalities or comparisons (ConjunctionOrFilter). Examples are disjunctive range predicates and the per-table OR filters derived by JoinDependentFilterRule. It does not apply to:
- VARCHAR/bool/interval columns
- non-flat (dictionary/constant) vectors
- expressions with casts, functions, IN, IS NULL, or NOT
- constants whose type differs from the column type
- vectors with more than STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE selected rows
All of these use the existing paths unchanged. Semantics match the executor: it uses the same Equals/LessThan/etc. operator templates (including NaN handling for floats), and a NULL row fails a NOT-free AND/OR tree.
structured_output.notes:
- Profile ToString looks the same for ConjunctionOrFilter and ExpressionFilter. Check which TableFilterType actually reaches FilterSelection before optimizing it.
- In the scan, the OR filter often runs after more selective filters (shipinstruct eq, the bloom-filter dynamic filter), so work must stay proportional to the incoming sel. Dense evaluation of the full vector cost +5%; gathering first fixed it.
- Possible follow-up: make TryPushdownOrClause build ConjunctionOr-of-ConjunctionAnd TableFilters for OR-of-ranges. That would also enable zonemap pruning through ConjunctionOrFilter::CheckStatistics, but it is a riskier plan-level change.
- The remaining lineitem scan cost in q19 is the other filters: the string-equality filter, the optional IN filter on another string column, and the bloom-filter dynamic filter.
